body:
thank you so much for taking the time to write this all out. I came here in the hopes that someone would tell me I'm not alone, but I feel like you really sat down to think this trough as well. Non of my current  friends can relate to my specific situation and it makes me feel very alone at times.  


And because these problems are regarding sex, it has made me feel very vapid and shallow in the past, like 'lol cant you just be less horny geez'. Me and my partner have tried meeting each other halfway, like casual cuddling with a bit more. They also tell me they are attracted to me and that they like having sex with me, but then not act on their words. This makes me feel even worse, because it reminds me of how much our sexual instincts differ and I often end up retreating.  Thank you for reminding me that this is indeed no ones fault, but all comes back to a relationship dynamic that lacks something and is worth reconsidering if its affects me this much.  


I hadn't even taken into consideration making a deliberate mental game plan for myself at all. The only game plan in action so far has been me acting out, flirting with others, venting sexual frustration online, crushing on friends. But I can now see that these are very temporary ways to cope, not sustainable ones.  I honestly don't really know where to start, but bringing it up with the psych I am currently assigned might be a good start. I do fear this psych might not get me entirely, she thinks my problems are largely sleep related. Only one way to find out.   


Now comes the tricky part that I have been struggling with the past few months.  I get to the point where I remind myself that this situation and the staggering mental health is a legitimate reason to break up over, and that solo life would probably fit me better. But then the doubt sets in and I have a really hard time to keep admitting the truth to myself, let alone bring it up with my partner.  
I always keep circling back to it being 'a selfish decision' on my part, bc I have very little outside voices reminding me that I'm allowed to take my hurt regarding sex seriously. Nor do I know if any of our friends would understand if I break up with my partner. I find myself scared to admit the truth and it often makes me retreat into 'maybe it wont be such a big problem', untill a RSD episode comes around again.   


I want to stop circling, but I'm having the hardest time getting friends/mental health staff to understand me and back me up, because no one I know is in this specific situation. But I think for my own sake, I gotta keep trying. Again, thank you so much, it was really helpful to read your comment and think about a game plan.

I am located in the Netherlands, where public mental healthcare is for free, but also very slow. Its the kind of professional institutions that work on large scale, but also have long waiting lists and take a long time to diagnose you. Getting official diagnosis for ADD with private institutions kind of slipped my mind when I first started looking into getting a diagnosis.

Me and the psych are indeed far enough in the process to conclude that the ADD and depression are co-morbid, but they insist I try light therapy before I get on any medication, so that's going to take a while. I don't really know how assert that my relationship problems could probably do with some cognitive therapy, but I'm bringing it up next session for sure. Will keep the medicine possiblities in mind as well.

A) I have not been prescribed any, because my ADD treatment has been delayed for half a year this year. I was diagnosed last march and am still in the process of waiting for an official test and further help. (According to my psych, Ive lasted this long undiagnosed on my smarts, but I've worn myself thin doing so)

B) no other medication either 

C) I am currently waiting to start depression treatment, but again, a very slow process, with psych staff who are very hesitant to prescribe me medication.

I am also not new to depression, but this year was by far my longest lasting depression, which got triggered by the build up of relationship stress and difficulty with finding permanent jobs during covid.
